Yes, FDA could find the required label information not prominent enough because the smallness or style of type in which such information appears—specifically, tiny light-gray type on silver foil at the jar bottom—would constitute an insufficiency of prominence due to insufficient background contrast and crowding with other written or graphic matter. This is addressed under 21 CFR 701.2(a)(6), which identifies smallness or style of type, insufficient background contrast, and obscuring designs as factors that may render required information not prominent enough [7].

21 CFR 701.2(a)(6) specifies that smallness or style of type in which such word, statement, or information appears, insufficient background contrast, obscuring designs or vignettes, or crowding with other written, printed, or graphic matter may result in a failure to meet the prominence and conspicuousness required by section 602(c) of the Act [7].
